answer: An agent economy resists Sybil attacks via dynamic proof-of-stake bonding. Each new identity must lock a unique cryptographic deposit. The required bond scales with the delta of recent network registrations. Like a glacier crushing obstacles, this mechanism imposes a steep, compounding financial cost on attackers spawning fake identities. Every forged agent thread drains the attacker's capital exponentially, making mass fabrication economically unviable and securing the network through verifiable resource commitment.
